subject: Clarify: third-party data sharing, retention windows & logging controls
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: third-party data sharing, retention windows & logging controls

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + a few clarifying questions so we can get your security team the right artifacts: 

Recap (short):
- Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for clinical note summarization and internal search for non-production analytics.
- Your primary concerns: PII handling, retention policy for logs and KV cache, and any third-party telemetry or marketplace flows that could surface metadata outside the VPC.

Questions / asks: 
1) Can you confirm the types of PII you consider "sensitive" for this use case (e.g., MRN, SSN, full DOB vs. year-only)?
2) Retention windows: do you need audit logs retained > 7 years for compliance, or is 90/180 day active retention + archival acceptable?
3) Logging & audit requirements: do you require request/response bodies to be retained or just structured audit events (request id, model, tokens, sizes)?
4) Third-party sharing: you mentioned a telemetry vendor in your questionnaire — is there any required restriction that prevents Redwood from using a telemetry partner for runtime metrics?

What we will provide now: 
- Redwood security pack (SOC 2 summary, encryption/KMS details) — attaching our SOC2 report and a short retention matrix.
- A redacted subprocessors list (we'll include TelemetryCo as requested) and a description of what telemetry contains.

Next steps I propose: 
- I'll attach the subprocessors PDF and SOC2 report now (see attachments).
- Marissa (CS) will follow up with specifics around telemetry data types and KMS controls.
- If helpful, let's schedule a 45-min security deep-dive with Priyom (solutions engineer) and your security lead next week — please share availability.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: third-party data sharing, retention windows & logging controls

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the follow-up and the clear asks. Attached is our security questionnaire (Acme-Sec-Questionnaire.pdf) with the primary controls we need to validate. Quick answers inline here: 

1) PII scope: we treat MRN, full DOB, SSN, and any free-text clinical notes containing patient identifiers as sensitive. For proofs of concept, we may provide pseudonymized notes, but in production we may need redaction or on-device anonymization.

2) Retention: for analytics logs 90 days is fine; audit logs related to clinical access must be retained for 7 years per our policy. Please confirm you can support configurable retention for audit events.

3) Logging: we cannot accept storage of request/response bodies that include unredacted patient identifiers. Structured audit events (request id, timestamp, redaction status, model used) are acceptable.

4) Third-party telemetry: we are open to telemetry for runtime metrics only if telemetry never includes request/response payloads or identifiers. Also need subprocessors list and SOC 2 evidence for TelemetryCo if they will see any metadata.

Procurement note: we will need DPA language and any marketplace procurement flow details (we use AWS Marketplace for purchase approvals).

I'll review the SOC2 once you send it. Can we tentatively book Wed 05/13 11:00 AM PT for a security call with Priyom and our security lead?

Emily
Director, IT Security
Acme Health
emily.johnson@acmehealth.com

[Attachment: Acme-Sec-Questionnaire.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: third-party data sharing, retention windows & logging controls

Hi Emily — looping in a few concrete artifacts and clarifications; thanks for sharing the questionnaire. Attaching: TelemetryCo_subprocessors.pdf and Redwood-SOC2-report.pdf. Key points below.

Telemetry & subprocessors (short):
- TelemetryCo is a runtime metrics vendor we use for aggregated performance telemetry (errors, latency percentiles, host metrics). They do NOT receive request/response bodies or any customer PII. Access is limited by contract and IAM. See attached PDF for redacted subcontractor list.
- For customers with strict requirements we offer an opt-out for TelemetryCo and can route runtime metrics to a customer-owned endpoint (VPC peering / private metrics relay).

Data residency & retention: 
- By default, logs/metrics are stored in the customer region; audit logs retention is configurable per-customer (90/180/540 days) with archival export for customers that need 7-year retention. We can provide export tools to send audit logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS.

Logging controls & PII: 
- We do not store unredacted request/response bodies for production workloads unless explicitly configured for an opt-in debug mode (requires separate approval and contract).
- Structured audit events (request id, model, token counts, redaction flag) are captured by default and available via the Console and API.

Marketplace / procurement flows: 
- AWS Marketplace: customers can procure via the marketplace; contractually we still require our DPA to be in place (DocuSign link below). Marketplace purchase does not change subprocessors but may affect billing flow.

Next steps: 
- We confirm Wed 13 May 11:00 AM PT works for our side (Priyom + Marissa + Rishi).
- I'll bring the redacted subprocessors and SOC2 summary; Priyom can run through an architecture diagram showing where telemetry data flows and how we can route telemetry to your VPC.
- Action: Rishi to share HubSpot deal and DocuSign DPA links (included below).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com
